title: Sharp Horvitz-Thompson Risk for Rooted-Forest Random Cluster Designs on Cycles
banked_reason: The note proves a sharp worst-case HT variance and unique fugacity optimizer for fair-label unit cycles; its weighted-tree and bounded-width results compute exposure probabilities but establish no risk or tuning guarantee on those graphs.
gap_reasons: The note proves a sharp worst-case HT variance and unique fugacity optimizer for fair-label unit cycles; its weighted-tree and bounded-width results compute exposure probabilities but establish no risk or tuning guarantee on those graphs.

The cycle improvement over size-two blocks is about 0.84%, and the maximizing outcome schedule has identical treatment and control endpoints, limiting the demonstrated value of this particular uncentered-HT criterion.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 completed the tree exposure certificate, cycle covariance and sharp-risk calculation, unique optimizer, rational separation, and exact finite-cycle certificate in the discovery note. D0.5 math and decision reviewers passed with no findings after explicit prior-art and dependency repairs, but the general review rated the delivered cycle-specific gain incremental, below the field floor. A sharp risk and comparator theory for a non-cycle graph family remains a separate research program; Lean formalization was not started.
tldr: Ugander et al.\ obtain size-three consecutive blocks on a full-neighborhood cycle with balanced labels, common treated response, and zero control response. Under the proved two-arm bounded-endpoint criterion, the partition-conditioned block frontier instead has unique size-two optimum \(32\). Fair-label rooted forests have sharp cycle risk \(R(z)\), uniquely minimized near fugacity \(1.7712563895\) at \(31.7317968506\); every \(4/3\le\lambda\le9/4\) is below \(32\), and exact arithmetic certifies the gain already at \(n=8\) for \(\lambda=25/14\). Colored determinants, cycle transfer, weighted-tree formulas, and a supplied-width dynamic program give auditable full-neighborhood exposure weights; exact sharp-null inference and a conservative interval use those weights.
gap: Forest determinants and cycle normalizers count uncolored partitions, while exposure HT needs colored marginal and pair events. Existing cluster-design theory includes sharp fixed-partition bias/MSE criteria and pseudoinverse variance bounds, but no inspected theorem gives the exact full-neighborhood two-arm HT worst-case constant and finite-cycle certificate for the rooted-forest law.
fill: Establish the corrected colored-assignment determinant, cycle transfer and weighted-tree pair formulas, and the supplied-width join invariant; prove covariance domination, the sharp cycle risk, uniform finite-cycle bound, unique optimizer, finite-n risk certificate, and named-family comparisons. Apply exact weights to sharp-null tests and a deterministic conservative interval.
